segments.text: In {1977|nineteen seventy-seven}, a telescope in Ohio heard something from space for seventy-two seconds. It has never been heard again.
A message from aliens? No chance. Let's go look.
The Big Ear telescope listens to the sky all night, and a computer prints what it hears.
Days later, volunteer Jerry Ehman reads the printout. He circles six characters and writes one word. Wow.
Look closer. The signal sits right by the frequency of hydrogen. Exactly where searchers expected a call.
They point the telescope back, again and again. Nothing. It never repeats.
In {2024|twenty twenty-four}, scientists propose a suspect. A hydrogen cloud that flared when a dead star's blast hit it.
So which is it? A glowing cloud of gas, or somebody saying hello?
Even they won't rule anything out. Your theory goes in the comments. This case stays open.
